title: How Are Thy Servants Blest, O Lord
description: How Are Thy Servants Blest, O Lord in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Joseph Addison wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 995 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Traveller's Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How are thy ser-vants blest, O Lord! How sure is their de-fence! E-ter-nal wis-dom is their guide, Their help om-ni-po-tence.

lines: How are thy servants blest, O Lord!
In foreign realms, and lands remote,
They pass unhurt through burning climes,
The hoary, frozen hills it warms,
In midst of dangers, fears, and death,
And praise thee for thy mercies past,

licence: Public domain: Joseph Addison died in 1719.
credits: Words by Joseph Addison (1672–1719), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
